topic: Super Simple Software Factory: Repeatable Agent Workflows as a Skill

key_points: Packages repeatable agents-plus-code workflows as a single Claude skill stamped into any repo
Deterministic Python (ADW — AI Developer Workflow) owns sequencing, retries, acceptance; agents are bounded nodes inside that graph
Core motto: 'Agent proposes, code disposes' — control plane lives in code, not in the prompt
Stamped repo layout: adws/ (adw_plan.py, adw_build.py, adw_test.py, adw_document.py, adw_simple_sdlc.py, adw_modules/), adw_data/prompt_engineering/ for tracked prompts, sssf.config.yaml agent roster
Same cursor query is both live view and full history transport (no ingest endpoint)
Software factory = structured, repeatable pipeline turning raw inputs (requirements, code, tests) into quality software
Division of labour: humans set strategy/frameworks/standards, AI handles retrieval/synthesis/formatting/execution
Three layers: Data layer (live sources like Jira/Confluence), Orchestration layer, Skills layer (AI playbooks)
Pattern: thin SKILL.md in a standard location pointing to full skill detail inside the factory for portability
Analogy to Gang of Four design patterns — shared vocabulary and captured expertise
Idea predates AI by decades: Bemer 1968 proposal, SDC 1975, Microsoft 2004 Software Factories book, BMW enterprise programs
2026 is an agent-native reinterpretation — autonomous systems do more planning/implementation/testing/review
Engineers define intent, acceptance criteria, govern access, and review evidence
Broader than a coding assistant (includes production system) and broader than CI/CD
Uber software factory: 70%+ of pull requests attributed to local/cloud agents, 3,600+ employee-built agent skills
Cost equation: benchmark-driven model routing, cheaper default models for subagents, prompt caching tuned to idle gaps, lean tool schemas
Code-mode subprocess loop: 50-71% token savings on trivial queries, ~100% on wide result sets, 90%+ on bulk workflows
Honest caveat: PRs are 'attributed to' agents with human review/escalation — agents drive work, not shipping 70% unreviewed
Built 30+ production workflow skills across the SDLC

stats.fact: 90% of professional developers used AI coding agents at work at least weekly by May-July 2026 (up sharply from early 2026)
stats.source: JetBrains State of Developer Ecosystem AI survey, 2026

stats.fact: Uber attributes more than 70% of pull requests to agents and has 3,600+ employee-built agent skills across the SDLC
84% of developers use or plan to use AI tools in 2026 (up from 76% in 2024), but only 29% trust AI outputs to be accurate (down from 40%)
46% of developers actively distrust AI accuracy, and 66% list 'almost right but not quite' as their top frustration
93% of IT leaders plan to deploy autonomous agents within 2 years; 33% of enterprise software will have built-in agentic capabilities by 2028
Anthropic's Claude skills pattern exploded in popularity — a single CLAUDE.md-driven skills approach reached ~176K GitHub stars by mid-2026

angles: The reliability gap: everyone can get an AI agent to write code once, almost nobody gets the same result twice — determinism is the moat
Move the control plane out of the prompt and into Python: 'agent proposes, code disposes'
Skills as the unit of reuse: packaging a repeatable workflow as a single skill stamped into any repo
Human vs agent division of labour: humans own intent, standards, and acceptance; agents own execution
The cost-engineering playbook from Uber: model routing, prompt caching, lean tool schemas
Trust collapse (29% trust accuracy) as the driver behind deterministic workflows over free-form agent use
